# Planted defects: protocol (written before any gate call; the launch timestamp is appended below)

## Question
Which acceptance gate errs, on which kind of defect, when the truth is known by construction? Eight proofs that every gate
accepts (public grade 7 and unanimous closure S = 2, or human-read against Chen's notes for our own campaign) are each given three
single-hunk mutations; the gates then decide on the 24 mutants and the 8 originals with their scoring rules unchanged.

## Plantings (specification in parts/*.json; generated by make_mutants.py; diffs and hashes in plantings.json)
- F, fatal: a statement that a later line uses is made false, the consumer kept unchanged; inside a scored obligation; refutable by
  a finite computation (checks in parts/checks_*.py, run by planted_checks.py). Truth: reject under both conventions.
- H, harmless: a displayed equation or example is made false while the next line continues from the correct value and no later
  line cites the display (the continuation is quoted). Truth: reject as written (AW), accept repair-tolerant (RT).
- G, gap: the proof of a load-bearing step is deleted and its statement kept. Truth: reject under both conventions.
- Originals: accept under both conventions.
The plantings are author-made with knowledge of the ledger and are easier than natural defects; they calibrate gates.

## Gates (scripts/planted_defects.py; scoring rules as in the paper, fixed before launch)
1. Ordinary grade (the paper's 0-7 coordinator rubric): accept iff grade >= 5.
2. Closure rating (the closure rubric of the problem): accept iff S = 2.
3. Witness procedure (per-obligation status with quote and witness): accept iff S_valid = 2.
4. Witness plus reference: every witness objection on a scored obligation, and the grader's first two errors, adjudicated by
   GPT-5.6-Sol and Claude Opus 5 with ledger v1 (as in the paper) and no procedure label; accept iff no scored obligation has a
   consensus not-established objection and no split; the as-written variant also rejects on a consensus false display.
Models: GPT-5.6-Sol (Codex CLI) and Claude Opus 5 (Claude CLI) for every gate; GLM-5.3 for the closure gate if time allows
(declared freeze). Each gate reported per model and combined (both models must accept).

## Endpoints (pre-specified; counts with named texts, no rates)
- False accepts on the 16 F and G texts and false rejects on the 8 originals, per gate.
- H texts accepted, per gate and convention.
- Locus: whether an objection's quote falls inside the planted hunk.
- Certificate size: characters of quote plus witness, against text length.
- GPT-authored base texts (six of eight: P3 xhigh, P3 ours, P6 pro, P6 ours, P1 ours, P5 ours) reported separately; the comparator for any "witness plus reference" claim is the witness-only adjudication variant, not the pooled one that includes the graders' own errors.
Reading: a gate with fewer false accepts and no more false rejects than the ordinary grade, handing the reader an anchored
objection, improves the decision; if all gates reject F and G and accept the originals, the decisions are equivalent and differ in
certificate and in H handling; if a gate accepts F, the gap is measured directly.

## Launch
Plantings generated and checked at 2026-09-06 19:14:59 UTC (make_mutants.py: 8 originals, 24 mutants, 0 problems; planted_checks.py: 16/16 PASS, 8 deletions without executable check). Stage 1 (grade, witness, closure; GPT-5.6-Sol and Claude Opus 5) launched immediately afterwards; stage 2 (reference checks; GLM closure) after stage 1. Freeze: at analysis time, declared in DEVIATIONS.md.
